card.statement:
A stability structure on $\cal A$ consists of a preorder $\preceq$ on the set of
objects of $\cal A$ satisfying the following properties:

- [(i)] trichotomy: for any two non-zero objects $A$ and $B$, either
$A\prec B$, or $B\prec A$, or $A\asymp B$;

- [(ii)] seesaw property: for each short exact sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$
of non-zero objects we have that:

$$ {\rm either}~~~ A\prec B \Longleftrightarrow
B\prec C \Longleftrightarrow A\prec C ~~,$$

$$ {\rm or}~~~ A\succ B \Longleftrightarrow
B\succ C \Longleftrightarrow A\succ C ~~,$$

$$ {\rm or}~~~ A\asymp B \Longleftrightarrow
B\asymp C \Longleftrightarrow A\asymp C ~~.$$

where:

- $A\asymp B$ if $A\preceq B$ and $B\preceq A$;

- $A\prec B$ if $A\preceq B$ but not $A\asymp B$;

- $A\succ B$ if $B\prec A$.
card.label: Definition 1

paper.title: On Moduli Spaces for Abelian Categories
paper.abstract: We show that if A is an abelian category satisfying certain mild conditions, then one can introduce the concept of a moduli space of (semi)stable objects which has the structure of a projective algebraic variety. This idea is applied to several important abelian categories in representation theory, like highest weight categories.
